activity.title: I'm happy to share that my team won 1st place at Hack the Town hackathon sponsored by Google Play , presented by Hack the Hood ! We won $1800 :) and what's more exciting is to see my first app published on the Google Play Store! This was a 2-day event and my first hackathon experience. We built TrashGO, a community-driven platform designed to make neighborhood cleanups more accessible, engaging, and rewarding. Our goal with TrashGO was to create a platform where anyone can report local trash, discover cleanup events, and organize meetups to work together to clean up their communities. A big inspiration behind TrashGO was Pokémon GO. We wanted to take this idea of people meeting together and catching Pokemon and apply it to cleaning up neighborhoods. We plan to build upon this with gamified points and a rewards system that encourages users to participate, stay active, and be engaged. We also want to collaborate with local restaurants and businesses to offer benefits for members. In just two days, we built the full user experience, including authentication, an interactive map, event pages, progress tracking, event creation, scheduling, location finder, personal activity tracking, and an impact dashboard! Since this was my first hackathon, I learned so much about building under a tight deadline, turning an idea into a working product, designing around user needs, and collaborating with an amazing team. The most important lesson I learnt is building a good product isn't just about writing code or coming up with a solution, rather finding a real problem that solves a need while contributing to a meaningful cause and it's broader impact. A huge thank you to our awesome coach, Zain Shafique , for guiding us throughout the hackathon, helping us work through the idea, and pushing us to build TrashGO. I'm incredibly grateful to have built this with my team Owen Cruz, Solomon, Jason, and Johann. This was an amazing first hackathon experience, and I can't wait to continue my adventure of ideating and building! A year ago, I probably would’ve laughed if you told me I’d be spending my summer trying to build a new approach to computing. But here we are. Excited to share that I’ve joined Entrepreneur First’s San Francisco fellowship program to continue building Sumeru Quantum! At Sumeru, we’re exploring a new approach to computing using superconducting digital logic, with the goal of building significantly more energy-efficient compute infrastructure for AI and HPC. We’ve been moving quickly from architecture to hardware, developing circuit-level simulations, designing our first superconducting test structures, and working toward fabrication and experimental validation. Along the way, I’ve had the opportunity to work with and learn from researchers and engineers across superconducting electronics, fabrication, and high-performance computing. Excited for what’s ahead 📈 ...more ...more

I'm happy to share that Neev Tamboli , Shivansh Bansal , and I won 1st place in 2 different tracks at the Daytona Hack Sprint! (1st overall and Best Use of Fireworks). We built a continuation of SubStrata, a satellite land-cover classification agent that gets more accurate over time. Aayush Gandhi , Neev Tamboli and I had built this project earlier, but we decided to build on it at this hackathon! Space agencies and research teams often rely on general-purpose land cover models that plateau in accuracy, and improving them typically requires either expensive proprietary retraining or slow, manual review by researchers. Substrata is a space agency oriented land cover classification tool that uses a recursive self-improvement loop between two AI models to push satellite imagery classification accuracy from 42% to 91%. Gemini 3.5 Flash classifies and segments Sentinel-2 and Dynamic World satellite imagery pulled through Google Earth Engine, while a second model audits its output against ground-truth labels, flags discrepancies, and pushes corrections into a persistent memory layer that Gemini references on every subsequent image. At this hackathon, we implemented Fireworks AI to host the vision classifier that scores every satellite patch, alongside using it to power LLM tool calls throughout the pipeline. We rebuilt our scoring system on Braintrust instead of relying on our own math, and the results spoke for themselves: our graph memory approach hit 89% accuracy versus 64% for raw retrieval. We also rebuilt our heuristic panel using CopilotKit, so you can watch the model write out its reasoning live and see the accuracy graph climb in real time as it learns. To make the whole system more resilient, we moved each batch into its own Daytona sandbox, so one bad batch can no longer take the entire pipeline down. Before submitting, we ran everything through CodeRabbit for a final review pass on the code we shipped. Special thanks to Sinan Ozdemir for guiding us through any problem we had! As always, I had a great time building this with Neev and Shivansh, and I can't wait to continue building more things like this in the future. I'm heading to London for the next few weeks but I can't wait to get back and start building! ...more ...more
